summary: An account's sign-ins joined by legs on a map, with the time and distance between them. A move faster than travel allows tears apart.

props.name: signIns
props.description: The account's sign-ins: `{ id, time, lat, lon, city?, device?, address? }`, in any order (they are sorted by time). `time` is epoch ms, an ISO 8601 string (read as UTC without an offset) or a Date. Entries with a duplicate id, an invalid time or an invalid position are skipped with a development warning. An empty array shows "No sign-ins yet".

props.name: maxKmh
props.description: Speeds above this, in km/h, are impossible.

props.name: minKm
props.description: Moves shorter than this, in km, are never flagged, since IP locations can be off by a few hundred kilometres.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when a sign-in is selected from the list or the map, or the selection is cleared.

props.name: onFlag
props.description: Called once per impossible leg when it first appears in the data: `{ from, to, km, hours, kmh }` with the two sign-in ids. `kmh` is Infinity when both sign-ins share a timestamp.

props.name: replay
props.description: Plays the legs in order on first view and when the data changes. Appended sign-ins play from the first new one.

props.name: unit
props.description: Unit of distances and speeds: km with km/h, or mi with mph. `maxKmh` and `minKm` stay in km.

props.name: timeZone
props.description: IANA time zone of the times in the list. Invalid zones fall back to UTC.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale for numbers and times. Without it, `en-US`.

methods.description: Plays the legs again in order from the first sign-in. Does nothing with reduced motion or `replay={false}`.

keyboard.action: Moves into the list, to the sign-in focused last, else the selected one or the first. The list is one tab stop.
Moves focus to the next or previous sign-in.
Moves focus to the first or last sign-in.
Selects the focused sign-in, or clears it when it is already selected.

accessibility: The root is a group labelled "Sign-in travel". The timeline is an ordered list labelled "Sign-ins, oldest first" with one native button per sign-in, using a roving tab index.

Each button is labelled with the place, the time, the device and the address, carries `aria-pressed` for the selection and is described by the leg that leads to it, for example "40 minutes later, 10,848 km away: impossible travel at 16,272 km/h."
A polite live region announces each impossible leg once, for example "Impossible travel: London to Singapore, 10,848 km in 40 minutes."
The map (canvases, markers, place names and speed chips) is `aria-hidden`; the list carries the same data. Markers respond to the pointer only.
motion: With reduced motion the land shows without its reveal, the legs appear complete without the replay, and impossible legs show a static dashed red gap with their chip, without the wobble or sparks. Rows do not flash and numbers change without rolling.
notes: Each leg is checked with the great-circle distance and the time between the two sign-ins: it is impossible when it covers more than `minKm` at more than `maxKmh`. Sign-ins within 25 km share one marker, with a count; a leg between them is not drawn and takes only a short beat in the replay.

The map is Equal Earth, centred on the sign-ins and zoomed until they fill the box with a margin; a single sign-in shows about 70 degrees around it. Calm legs bend slightly to the left of travel, so a return trip runs beside the outward one.

The replay draws each leg in 0.6 s with a packet at its head. A point pings the land dots around it as it is reached and its row lights up. An impossible leg draws to its midpoint, tears there and opens a 7 px gap on a spring; red sparks crackle in the gap for 1.4 s, the chip with the speed and the time pops in, and the far half grows back from the destination.

Selecting a sign-in, in the list or on the map, draws its incoming and outgoing legs larger, dims the rest and shows the incoming route and speed under the map. Selecting an end of a torn leg crackles its gap again. Clicking a marker repeatedly steps through the sign-ins at that place; clicking the empty map clears the selection.
Times in the list use `formatZonedTime` with a short date. The time between sign-ins is written with `min` for minutes, so it does not read as metres next to a distance.
A note under the list says that locations are approximate, since they come from IP addresses.

data.note: Pass your sign-ins as `signIns`. Without it the component shows six invented demo sign-ins.
